summary: Read KMY arXiv:2404.14628v2 (Duke, to appear): Thm 1 N(α;Q)=Ψ(Q)+O(Ψ^{1/2+ε}) for a.e. α, via Thm 2 ∫(N−Ψ)² ≤ Ψ+O(Ψ^{1+ε}); the key overlap Lemma 5.1 bounds λ(A_q∩A_r) ≤ 1[D≥1/2]λ(A_q)λ(A_r)e^{2L_t(q,r)}2^{ω_t(q,r)}(1+O(log(4D)/D)), D=max(rψ(q),qψ(r))/gcd(q,r) — a metric (a.e. α) statement, i.e. B6, and no specific/rational α is covered. ES translation (PROVED, elementary): for the trial-form events {n ≡ −u mod m}, m=4uC−1, the exact overlap ratio is gcd(m,m')·1[u≡u' mod gcd]; same-u pairs are always compatible, so the ratio is gcd(4uC−1, C'−C) with no penalty, which gives divisor-function-type positive correlation. CERTIFIED numerics (scripts/z52d_p2_ZF1_Z2411_var.c, windows of 1–2·10⁶ at X=10⁶,10⁷,10⁸,10⁹): Var R/mean R over primes p≡1(4) is 3.91, 4.57, 5.38, 6.14 (all odd n: 4.64, 5.46, 6.44, 7.49), and after removing class means mod 840 it is still 2.74, 3.37, 4.16, 4.92. It grows ≈0.33·log X, so the KMY-type quasi-independence (Var ≤ M^{1+ε}) FAILS for the ES event system (EVIDENCE: Var ≍ M log X ≍ M^{3/2}); same-u pairs with u ≤ 2000 explain 13→33 of the excess Var−2·mean = 70→196 (10⁶→10⁸). A KMY/Chebyshev second moment would therefore give at best #{n≤X: R(n)=0} ≪ X/log X, far weaker than Vaughan. This extends Z3109 (which stopped at 10⁵) to 10⁹.
not_done: I did not read KMY §§8–15 (GCD-graph iteration) in detail, and I did not compute the full Fourier/d-decomposition of the cross-u covariance (only the same-u part with u ≤ 2000 and the mod-840/9240 class-mean part). No GCD-graph bound for ES moduli was attempted, because the measured over-dispersion already rules out the target inequality.
next: If a second moment is ever wanted, weight the events by a divisor-correcting factor (e.g. 1/τ-type damping per u) and re-measure Var/mean before importing any GCD-graph machinery.

summary: Verified Heath-Brown, Acta Arith. 72 (1995) 235–275, Thm 1 (read in the original PDF): Σ*_{m≤M}|Σ*_{n≤N} a_n (n/m)|² ≪_ε (MN)^ε(M+N)Σ*|a_n|², where m and n run over odd squarefree integers and a_n is INDEPENDENT of m (Cor 1–3 cover all real primitive characters and non-squarefree n). ES side (derivation from BM_CORRECTED_COUNT §1–2, Thm 1.1(3), Prop 2.1(d,e)): R(p) = M_BM(p) + X_BM(p), where X_BM collects every character mod q=4uB except 1 and χ_{−4uB}. In X_BM the modulus is q and the argument is the single point p, so at fixed p there is no mean square for HB to act on: HB with one modulus is plain Cauchy–Schwarz, and the non-real characters, which carry the lower-tail problem, lie outside HB altogether. The item's own form (modulus 4C, argument d | 4Cp+1) breaks HB's hypothesis that a_d does not depend on the modulus; this is exactly the tied-modulus B2 coupling. The only place where HB's roles fit is the BM term T(p) = Σ_{m≤p/4, 2|m} (−m/p)2^{ω(m)}/(4φ(m)), with modulus p averaged over primes and argument m. There the loss can be stated exactly (scripts/z52d_p2_ZF1_Z1448_hb.py, 300 primes ≡ 1 (4) after P0 = 10⁴, 10⁵, 10⁶): the true mean T² is 2.09, 2.95, 3.60, while the HB shape gives (1+N/M)Σ|a|² = 1.41–1.43 times (MN)^ε·log M (EVIDENCE). So HB is sharp up to P^ε but averaged only (B6), and it is superseded by the PROVED pointwise T(p) = (σ/4)E·L(1,χ_p)² + O(p^{−1/16}log p) (BM_LVALUE Thm A); Elliott's ε-free form (6) is useless here, with shape ~10³–10⁶.
not_done: I did not attempt HB's method (Poisson summation in m plus a recursive bound) for the genus characters (d/·), d | 4uB, beyond χ_{−4uB}, i.e. for M_gen − M_BM. Numerically that is O(few) at the 14 (★)-failures (BM_LVALUE §1.4: M_gen 29.08 vs M_BM 30.51 at 8 813 281), and it is also only an average. I did not run windows beyond 300 primes per scale.
next: None for ES pointwise. An averaged second moment of M_gen − M₀ over p would be a citeable corollary of HB Cor 2, but B6 applies to it.

summary: I ran 7 web and 4 arXiv-API searches (logged). No theorem was found on the equidistribution of ray classes of the ideal factors of a moving element at a fixed prime with growing conductor. The adjacent theorems found and checked are Birch 1968 vertical Sato–Tate (fixed p, all curves over F_p, equidistribution only as p→∞), Bhargava 2007 fixed-prime splitting densities over fields ordered by discriminant, and Duke–Friedlander–Iwaniec 1995/Tóth (roots ν/ℓ of a FIXED quadratic mod primes ℓ equidistribute mod 1; Weyl form bound (1.2) read in Ngo arXiv:2107.13301 §1). ES-side derivation (PROVED, elementary): DFI IS a fixed-p 'horizontal' theorem for the family, with f(X) = 4dX² + p² (disc −16dp² < 0); a prime Type I divisor ℓ of p²+4c²d with ℓ ≡ −p (mod 4cd) forces c ≡ ν_ℓ (mod ℓ), so c = ν_ℓ whenever ℓ > c (i.e. unless c(4dk−1) ≤ p, where ℓ = 4cdk−p). The event then reads ν_ℓ/ℓ = (1+p/ℓ)/(4dk) EXACTLY, an exact rational point that equidistribution at any scale ≫ 1/ℓ cannot see (B3). Premise check: the ray-class phrasing is correct but over-structured, since only the norm class f mod 4cd matters; moreover every coprime factor f has χ_{−4d}(f) = 1, so the target −p is reachable only when (−d/p) = −1, the known Type I parity law (FRONTIER §3 positivity, (J)89 Lemma 4.1).
not_done: Did not ask on MathOverflow (outreach; not done by a worker). Did not read DFI's proof or Bhargava's mass formulae in full; no numerical test, since the derivation shows the event is an exact-value condition that no equidistribution statement addresses.
next: If pursued, the right literature target is 'joint distribution of (ν_ℓ, ℓ mod ν_ℓ)' for roots of a fixed quadratic congruence; this is the B2 event in DFI coordinates.

summary: Bach–Sorenson (Math. Comp. 65 (1996)) verified via Lamzouri–Li–Soundararajan arXiv:1309.3595 §1.2: on GRH P(a,q) ≤ (1+o(1))(φ(q)log q)², explicitly P(a,q) ≤ 2(q log q)² (LLS sharpen this to (φ(q)log q)² for q>3). The engine is the explicit formula for S(x,χ) = Σ_{n≤x}Λ(n)χ(n)log(x/n) together with the zero-sum identity Σ_ρ 1/|ρ_χ|² = 2|Re B(χ)| ≤ log q + O(1) under GRH (LLS Lemma 2.2), so each non-principal χ contributes ≪ √x log q against a main term x. ES analogue (derivation): in the finite expansions of R(p) (pair form 1[p≡a (q)], divisor form D_{−1}(4Cp+1) = φ(4C)⁻¹Σ_χ χ(−1)σ_χ(N)) no inner averaging variable exists, and σ_χ(N) is a finite Euler product with no zeros, so the BS architecture degenerates to the triangle-inequality certificate Σ_{χ≠1}|σ_χ(N)| < τ(N). That certificate forces EVERY class of (ℤ/4C)^× to contain a divisor (needs τ(N) ≥ φ(4C)), i.e. a full-coset cover, which is B4 (LONGSHOT_PIGEONHOLE Thm 2.2). Test (scripts/z52d_p2_ZF1_Z2077_bscrit.py, C ≤ 60, all p ≡ 1 (4) in [10³,3·10³), [10⁵,1.1·10⁵), [10⁷,10⁷+6000)): the certificate fires for 122/135, ~406/424, 169/176 primes, almost always at C=1–3, and coincides with full coverage at 193/194, 801/809, 390/398 eligible levels. True (★) hits at C ≤ 60 miss only 4, ~4, 3 primes, and the (★)-failures 409…8 813 281 tested are uncertified.
not_done: Primary BS PDF (AMS/JSTOR/Butler repository) was Cloudflare-blocked; theorem statements verified only through LLS's citation (1.1)–(1.2) and LLS's own Lemma 2.2, not BS's text. Counts at 10⁵ include one duplicated prime (102001). No C > 60 levels.
next: Side remark only: on GRH, LLS Thm 1.4 gives an explicit polylog bound for the single Dirichlet prime r ≡ 3 (4), (n/r) = −1 that certifies the ES^□ relaxation (FRONTIER §3 B-fin); not ES itself.

summary: Premise is FALSE as stated: no Hooley (or other) GRH theorem for x²+y²+z³ was found. Jagy–Kaplansky, Exp. Math. 4 (1995) 169–173 (abstract read) record that all integers are x²+y²+z³ with mixed signs, that the all-positive problem is open with computations suggesting finitely many exceptions, and that x²+y²+z⁹ has infinitely many. The real Hooley GRH theorem is n = p + u² + v² (Acta Math. 97 (1957) 189–210; Thm 1 read, p. 209). On ERH the count is (πn/log n)·∏(1+χ₄(ℓ)/(ℓ(ℓ−1)))·∏_{ℓ|n}(explicit factor), and the singular series is bounded below for every n (no local obstruction; main term ≫ n/(log n log log n)). The method is Σ_p r(n−p) = 4Σ_d χ₄(d)π(n;n,d), a Titchmarsh divisor problem with a FIXED character χ₄, GRH on average over d ≲ √n, and a Brun-sieve treatment of the sign changes for the remaining d. Comparison with ES local densities (derivation from FRONTIER §2.1–2.2): the ES fibre over C is the hyperbola (4uC−1)(4BC−1) = 4Cn+1, whose count D⁻_{4C}(4Cn+1) = φ(4C)⁻¹Σ_{χ mod 4C}χ(−1)σ_χ(N) involves all characters to a modulus that moves with the fibre (Hooley: one fixed χ₄ per fibre). Its local factor M_BM is 0 or 2/φ(4uB) per pair and vanishes identically at odd squares, with total size ≍ log²p (Hooley: ≍ n/log n, i.e. M1a). Hooley's averaged variable is the prime p, independent of the modulus d; in ES the only long variable u (or C) sits inside the class modulus 4u — exactly the tied-modulus obstruction (FRONTIER §3, Remark 3.1). So neither the GRH input nor the sieve transfers.
not_done: I did not read Jagy–Kaplansky's full text (abstract only) or Hooley's §§2–4 sieve details. I did not search for post-1995 progress on the positive x²+y²+z³ problem beyond the web and arXiv queries listed, and ran no ES numerics (the comparison is structural).
next: None; if a mixed-degree analogue is wanted, the right sibling is Hooley/Linnik p+u²+v² (fixed-character Titchmarsh divisor problem), already covered by the B2/tied-modulus analysis.

summary: Formulation (derivation): {p : R(p)=0} is the set of primes left after sifting by one class −u mod m for every (u,C), m = 4uC−1 (τ((m+1)/4) classes per modulus m, total sifting density Σω(m)/m ≍ log²x), i.e. a large-sieve problem of growing dimension, which is Vaughan's route, not an FI/HB prime-detection problem. FI/HB need Type II because x²+y⁴ and x³+2y³ are THIN; the (★) sequence a_n = R(n) is DENSE (Σ_{n≤x}R(n) ≍ x log²x) and is a union of long APs n ≡ −u (mod 4uC−1). So Type I information holds to level ≈ x^{1−ε}, and Type II sums Σα_mβ_k R(mk) are controlled classically by characters mod q and the large sieve for q ≤ x^{1/2}. That information exists but only yields Σ_{p≤x}R(p) (BV-level averages, B6); the pointwise question lives in the fibres with q ≍ p, which carry O(1) elements (FRONTIER §3 tied modulus; consistent with BRAINSTORM/corr_parity_layers.md §4, 'parity is mis-targeted'). New census (CERTIFIED, scripts/z52d_p2_ZF1_Z2356_zeroset.c, all odd n ≤ 10⁸): the zero set 𝒵 has 6008 elements = 4999 odd squares + 1009 non-squares. Its 24 primes are exactly the 14 known p ≡ 1 (4) failures plus 10 p ≡ 3 (4), last 8 813 281. The non-square zeros per decade are 7, 20, 68, 145, 239, 299, 229 (last decade [10⁷,10⁸) declining), and their Ω is parity-balanced: 479 odd vs 530 even. A parity-blind upper-bound sieve can therefore bound primes in 𝒵 only down to the non-square composite zeros; the declining counts (EVIDENCE) suggest that set may be finite too, so the parity barrier is not the binding obstruction.
not_done: I did not re-read FI's or Heath-Brown's papers (verified as citations in BRAINSTORM/z52_lit_thin_pointwise.md). I did not prove the Type I/II statements above in detail (Assessment-level, standard), and did not extend the 𝒵 census beyond 10⁸.
next: Extend the non-square (★)-zero census to 10⁹–10¹⁰ (the existing (★) engines) to test whether 𝒵 \ squares is finite; that is the parity-relevant datum.
